rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 6 (kp 6.5, kd 0.6, 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.030 m, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, last_direction) is the best raced design at 122.66. All 60 trials still went off track. Oval steering_oscillation was 0.270 and oval max_error was 0.064, just over the 0.06 limit. Line losses were 1.3 (oval), 1.6 (s-bend) and 1.0 (slalom). Iteration 7 changed kd to 0.5 with kp 6.5 and scored worse at 91.44. Its oval oscillation was 0.265, still above 0.2, and its line losses rose on the oval (1.55). So lowering kd did not reduce oscillation, and it cost score. The Evaluator's R1 feedback describes the same kd 0.5 change, which has already raced, so I have treated it as stale for this iteration. Across kp 6.5 to 7.0 and kd 0.4 to 0.6, oval oscillation has stayed at 0.25 to 0.27. That suggests kp and kd are not the main driver. Still, the plan agreed earlier says that when oscillation stays above 0.2 at kd 0.5, return kd to 0.6 and reduce kp toward 6.0 rather than adding damping. Body width cannot relax the off-track limit, so control must hold max_error under 0.06.

Change. I return kd to 0.6, the best-scoring value, and reduce kp from 6.5 to 6.0. Geometry, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05 and last_direction are unchanged, so the result isolates the gain change against the best raced design (iteration 6).

Expected result. Oval steering_oscillation falls toward 0.25 or below with the lower edge gain. max_error may rise slightly, so the risk is off-track earlier on the oval. Progress should hold on the oval and s-bend.

Hypotheses. (1) The oscillation is set by edge response and sensor-edge transients, so a lower kp reduces jitter. (2) Line losses at the s-bend entries are the next limit on progress. If they persist at the same entries after this step, the next lever is line_loss search_left or search_right.

Next steps after the race. If oscillation drops and max_error is still at or above 0.06, widen the sensor array to x = ±0.040 m (16 mm sensors) and test kp near 8.0 with kd 0.6. If oscillation stays above 0.2 at kp 6.0, the jitter is not gain-driven, so test ki or sensor footprint changes rather than further kp cuts. If line losses stay at 1 or more at the same bend entries, change line_loss toward the side the failing bends turn.

Measurements wanted: steering_oscillation, max_error, line_loss_events, progress and completion_time per track, plus rms_error and control_effort.
